freeze verb

in the freeze game

also freeze game

classical

Lewis & Short

rigēscō, rigēscere, riguī

verb, third conjugation

stiffen, freeze

Mainly poetic (L&S). For the Medusa version of the game, Ovid’s line on the Gorgon (Met. 5.209).

Examples

  • Rigēsce!

    Freeze!composed

  • Obrigēsce!

    Freeze!composed

  • Gorgone bis centum riguērunt corpora vīsā

    two hundred bodies froze stiff at the sight of the GorgonOv. Met. 5.209

Other words

  • obrigēscō, obrigēscere, obriguī — freeze stiff

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cicero

  • rigeō, rigēre — be stiff, frozen

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.69 (with cold)

See also melt, you’re stone, don’t move.

SourcesLewis & Short: rigeo · Lewis & Short: rigesco · Lewis & Short: obrigesco

Vergil and Ovid checked against the Perseus Latin texts.

No ancient name for this game is known; the calls are our own, built on the classical verbs.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
